Attack_scenario: Attacker reaches Nginx directly and bypasses WAF
Required_controls: Authenticated origin pull or mTLS; firewall Cloudflare source allowlist; reject missing origin authentication

Attack_scenario: Client-supplied X-Forwarded-* changes IP, scheme or host interpretation
Required_controls: Nginx overwrites proxy headers; Django ALLOWED_HOSTS, SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER only for trusted proxy; strict CSRF origins

Attack_scenario: Traffic from separate Nginx VM is observed or altered
Required_controls: Private routed network plus verified upstream TLS/mTLS or WireGuard; rotate keys
Verification: MITM attempt and certificate mismatch test

Attack_scenario: Single reverse proxy causes total outage
Required_controls: Document RTO/RPO; backup config; tested rebuild; second proxy and LB for HA
Verification: Kill proxy VM and time recovery

Attack_scenario: Exposed VM yields routing control and secret theft
Required_controls: Harden OS, no app credentials, restricted SSH, patching, file integrity and centralized logs
Verification: Host hardening and secret exposure review

Attack_scenario: Upload and API floods exhaust gateway or app capacity
Required_controls: Edge and Nginx limits, per-route rate limits, upload directly to video provider

Attack_scenario: Reused passwords compromise accounts
Required_controls: Rate limits, breached-password screening, MFA for privileged roles, anomaly detection

Attack_scenario: Stolen access/refresh token accesses another account
Required_controls: Short access TTL, rotating refresh tokens, revocation, secure storage, device/session audit

Attack_scenario: Viewer accesses creator or moderator resources by changing IDs
Required_controls: Object-level authorization in each service; default deny; scoped service tokens

Attack_scenario: Moderator action lacks immutable audit context
Required_controls: Append-only audit trail with actor, target, reason, request ID and timestamp
Verification: Remove logs locally and verify central copy

Attack_scenario: Reset/login responses reveal registered users
Required_controls: Generic responses and uniform timing; per-IP/account rate limiting

Attack_scenario: Compromised container calls internal points endpoint as engagement service
Required_controls: Workload identity, short-lived service credentials, mTLS or signed service JWT with audience and scopes
Verification: Call points endpoint with wrong service identity

Attack_scenario: One service accesses unrelated private services
Required_controls: Segment overlay networks, per-service network membership, egress policies where supported

Attack_scenario: Exposed control plane yields full cluster control
Required_controls: Dedicated managers, restricted 2377, mutual node auth, hardened hosts, RBAC via operational access
Verification: Management port scan and admin access review

Attack_scenario: Secrets exposed through env, logs or backups
Required_controls: Swarm secrets or external manager; avoid env; rotation; encrypted backups; no secrets in images

Attack_scenario: Malicious dependency or image enters release
Required_controls: Pinned image digests, SBOM, SCA, signed provenance, approval gates
Verification: Deploy unsigned image in staging; block

Attack_scenario: Manager quorum or worker capacity unavailable
Required_controls: 3 managers for HA if budget permits; placement constraints; backup/restore; capacity alerting

Attack_scenario: Cannot attribute cross-service modification
Required_controls: Trace IDs propagated, immutable audit events, synchronized time

Attack_scenario: Client claims a video was uploaded without provider verification
Required_controls: Server-issued one-time upload intent; provider status lookup and signed webhook verification

Attack_scenario: Unauthorized user retrieves unpublished or removed video
Required_controls: Signed playback tokens where applicable; strict publish state; purge invalidation

Attack_scenario: Crafted file exploits transcoder or metadata parser
Required_controls: Managed provider processing, content-type/size checks, malware scanning where feasible, sandboxed parsing

Attack_scenario: Attacker replays provider callback to alter media status
Required_controls: Verify signature, timestamp, event ID deduplication and authoritative provider state

Attack_scenario: Bots or coordinated clients create fake qualified views
Required_controls: Server-validated watch evidence, device/network velocity rules, anti-abuse holds, no client point award

Attack_scenario: Duplicate watch/like events award repeated points
Required_controls: Idempotency keys, unique constraints, atomic transaction and dedupe windows

Attack_scenario: Creator boosts own content with controlled accounts
Required_controls: Self-view exclusion, collusion/velocity heuristics, review and reversals

Attack_scenario: Cannot explain why points were awarded or withheld
Required_controls: Versioned qualification rules, evidence reference, decision reason, trace ID

Attack_scenario: Client or unrelated service calls points write endpoint
Required_controls: Points ledger private network and service-auth; no public mutation route; allowlisted callers

Attack_scenario: Reversals and concurrent updates corrupt points balance
Required_controls: Append-only entries, idempotent postings, transactional constraints, derived balance and reconciliation

Attack_scenario: API leaks device/IP fingerprints or detection thresholds
Required_controls: Minimize retention, restrict analyst access, redact APIs and logs

Attack_scenario: Ad impression or click callback creates creator reward
Required_controls: Hard separation of ad telemetry and eligibility; no ad event ledger writer; architecture test
Verification: Send ad callback; assert zero points

Attack_scenario: Future payouts use unverified estimated earnings
Required_controls: No payouts in R1; later use collected eligible settled revenue, dual approval and reconciliation

Attack_scenario: Insider deletes or suppresses content beyond scope
Required_controls: Least privilege, dual review for sensitive bulk actions, reason codes, audit

Attack_scenario: Reporter/target personal data disclosed to other users
Required_controls: Case-level access, redaction, purpose limitation, retention policy

Attack_scenario: Database accepts public connections or weak credentials
Required_controls: Private DB network, per-service DB roles, TLS, least privilege, no public port

Attack_scenario: Content service modifies points tables directly
Required_controls: Separate logical databases/schemas and roles; API-only ownership; migration ownership

Attack_scenario: Backup object storage exposes account or audit data
Required_controls: Encrypted backups, least privilege, separate credentials, retention, restore testing

Attack_scenario: Jobs disappear or malicious payload executes
Required_controls: Authenticated private Redis, durable queues where required, schema validation, DLQ, retries
Verification: Worker crash/retry and invalid payload tests

Attack_scenario: Attacker publishes malicious image or Swarm stack
Required_controls: OIDC short-lived credentials, branch protection, two-person production approval, secret scanning

Attack_scenario: Central logs leak sessions or sensitive identifiers
Required_controls: Structured redaction, log access policy, retention, audit
Verification: Seed test secret; assert absent in logs

Attack_scenario: Backup exists but cannot restore data and service
Required_controls: Restore runbooks, periodic drills, point-in-time recovery, documented RTO/RPO

Attack_scenario: Attacker marks ticket paid without settlement
Required_controls: Deferred R3; signed webhooks, authoritative PSP lookup, idempotency

Attack_scenario: Insider approves own payout or changes beneficiary
Required_controls: Deferred R4; segregation of duties, double-entry money ledger, dual approval
